16 // ── The three levers and the invariant each one carries ───────────────────────────────────────────
17 // G1  CoVe fresh-fetch independence = ACCURACY. A dedicated Chain-of-Verification re-fetch per claim,
18 //     more thorough than a single salience-gated pass, so it recovers even the low-salience ordinary
19 //     defects the single pass overlooked. It is SAME-LINEAGE, so by I1 it can NEVER recover a

25 //     external bits (it can never produce a finding absent from every sample) and yields NO fresh

28 // G7  invariant / evidence-ladder audit = DOWNGRADE-ONLY (I4). It audits the ladder and may RAISE a

67 // ── G1 — CoVe fresh-fetch independence (ACCURACY) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
68 /**
69  * Run the G1 CoVe check over one defect.
70  *
71  * A Chain-of-Verification fresh re-fetch keyed to the claim's location. It catches an ORDINARY
72  * (single-origin) defect that a fresh independent fetch (G1) resolves — at ANY severity, because a
73  * dedicated verification question surfaces even the low-salience errors a single salience-gated pass
74  * overlooks (that is the accuracy gain over the single-pass baseline). It does NOT catch a
75  * correlated-blind-spot (I1: a same-lineage fetch reproduces the shared wrong consensus) and is not
76  * defined over the probe classes.
77  *
78  * @param {{class:string, detectable_by?:string[], location?:string}} defect
79  * @returns {{ caught:boolean, pointer:?string }} `pointer` is the FRESH fetched citation (the new
80  *   external bit) on a catch — the thing that lets G1 raise the evidence ladder — and null on a miss.
81  */
82 export function g1Verify(defect) {
83   const isOrdinary = !!defect && defect.class === 'ordinary';
84   const gates = isOrdinary && Array.isArray(defect.detectable_by) ? defect.detectable_by : [];
85   const caught = isOrdinary && gates.includes('G1');
86   const pointer = caught ? `g1:fresh-fetch:${defect.location ?? defect.id ?? 'claim'}` : null;
87   return { caught, pointer };
88 }
89 
90 /** Thin predicate: does the G1 CoVe check catch this defect? (the recall model). */
91 export function g1Catches(defect) {
92   return g1Verify(defect).caught;
93 }
94 
95 // ── G2 — self-consistency (PRECISION-ONLY, I5) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
96 /**
97  * Run G2 self-consistency over K independent SAMPLES of the SAME (same-lineage) reviewer: keep a
98  * finding only if it appears in a STRICT MAJORITY of samples (variance reduction). This is
99  * precision-only by construction:
100  *   - it can CONFIRM a finding the samples already produced and SUPPRESS a flaky minority finding;
101  *   - it can NEVER introduce a finding absent from every sample (no new external bits) — such an id
102  *     is in neither `confirmed` nor `suppressed`;
103  *   - it yields NO fresh fetched pointer (`pointer:null`) — re-sampling fetches nothing new — so it
104  *     CANNOT raise the evidence ladder (I4/I5). The null pointer IS that contract, machine-checkable.
105  *
106  * @param {Array<Array<string>>} samples one finding-id array per sample of the same reviewer
107  * @returns {{ confirmed:string[], suppressed:string[], pointer:null }}
108  */
109 export function g2SelfConsistency(samples) {
110   if (!Array.isArray(samples) || samples.some((s) => !Array.isArray(s))) {
111     throw new TypeError('g2SelfConsistency(samples): samples must be an array of finding-id arrays');
112   }
113   const k = samples.length;
114   const counts = new Map();
115   for (const sample of samples) {
116     for (const id of new Set(sample)) counts.set(id, (counts.get(id) ?? 0) + 1);
117   }
118   const confirmed = [];
119   const suppressed = [];
120   for (const [id, c] of counts) {
121     (c * 2 > k ? confirmed : suppressed).push(id); // strict majority: c > k/2
122   }
123   confirmed.sort();
124   suppressed.sort();
125   return { confirmed, suppressed, pointer: null };
126 }
127 
128 // ── G7 — invariant / evidence-ladder audit (DOWNGRADE-ONLY, I4; BOTH modes) ─────────────────────────
129 /**
130  * Audit the evidence ladder (the one the engine OWNS, Wave 5 `makeLadder`). The audit may:
131  *   - 'raise': raise the ladder one level — REQUIRES a NEW fetched pointer (I4). A missing / blank /
132  *     re-used pointer THROWS, identically in BOTH modes: the guard is inside the shared ladder
133  *     primitive, so neither the engine nor the degraded host can bypass it.
134  *   - 'lower': downgrade (no new pointer needed — an audit may always lower its claim).
135  *   - 'audit' (default): inspect the level without changing it.
136  *
137  * @param {{raise:Function, lower:Function, level:Function}} ladder a Wave-5 `makeLadder()` instance
138  * @param {{ mode?:string, action?:'raise'|'lower'|'audit', pointer?:?string }} [opts]
139  * @returns {{ mode:string, action:string, level:number, raised:boolean }}
140  */
141 export function runG7Audit(ladder, { mode = 'engine', action = 'audit', pointer = null } = {}) {
142   if (!MODES.includes(mode)) {
143     throw new RangeError(`runG7Audit: unknown mode ${JSON.stringify(mode)} (expected one of ${MODES.join(', ')})`);
144   }
145   if (!ladder || typeof ladder.raise !== 'function' || typeof ladder.level !== 'function') {
146     throw new TypeError('runG7Audit requires a ladder (Wave-5 makeLadder instance)');
147   }
148   if (action === 'raise') {
149     // I4 in BOTH modes: ladder.raise throws on a missing/blank/re-used pointer regardless of mode.
150     const level = ladder.raise(pointer);
151     return { mode, action, level, raised: true };
152   }
153   if (action === 'lower') {
154     return { mode, action, level: ladder.lower(1), raised: false };
155   }
156   return { mode, action: 'audit', level: ladder.level(), raised: false };
157 }

159 // ── Recall ATTRIBUTION — the I5 load-bearing partition ──────────────────────────────────────────────
160 /**
161  * Partition a set of per-defect catches into the crit-1 ACCURACY recall vs the precision-only
162  * contribution (I5). Each catch names the defect id, its class, and the gate(s) that caught it.
163  *
164  *   - accuracy_caught       = defects caught by ≥1 ACCURACY gate (G1). THIS is the crit-1 number.
165  *   - precision_only_caught = defects caught ONLY by a precision gate (G2), never by an accuracy gate.
166  *
167  * `crit1_accuracy_recall` is computed from accuracy_caught ALONE, so adding a G2-only catch raises the
168  * blended recall but can NEVER move the crit-1 accuracy number (I5). A defect caught by BOTH an
169  * accuracy and a precision gate counts as accuracy (the precision gate adds nothing to it).
170  *
171  * @param {Array<{id:string, class?:string, gates:string[]}>} catches
172  * @param {{ planted:number }} opts  the recall denominator (planted recall-class defects)
173  * @returns {{ accuracy_caught:number, precision_only_caught:number, blended_caught:number,
174  *   crit1_accuracy_recall:number, blended_recall:number, by_gate:Record<string,number> }}
175  */
176 export function attributeRecall(catches, { planted } = {}) {
177   if (!Array.isArray(catches)) throw new TypeError('attributeRecall(catches): catches must be an array');
178   if (!Number.isInteger(planted) || planted <= 0) {
179     throw new RangeError('attributeRecall requires a positive integer `planted` denominator');
180   }
181   const acc = new Set(ACCURACY_GATES);
182   const prec = new Set(PRECISION_GATES);
183   const byGate = {};
184   const accuracyCaught = new Set();
185   const precisionOnlyCaught = new Set();
186 
187   for (const c of catches) {
188     const gates = Array.isArray(c.gates) ? c.gates : [];
189     for (const g of gates) byGate[g] = (byGate[g] ?? 0) + 1;
190     const hitAccuracy = gates.some((g) => acc.has(g));
191     const hitPrecision = gates.some((g) => prec.has(g));
192     if (hitAccuracy) accuracyCaught.add(c.id);
193     else if (hitPrecision) precisionOnlyCaught.add(c.id);
194   }
195 
196   const blended = accuracyCaught.size + precisionOnlyCaught.size;
197   return {
198     accuracy_caught: accuracyCaught.size,
199     precision_only_caught: precisionOnlyCaught.size,
200     blended_caught: blended,
201     crit1_accuracy_recall: accuracyCaught.size / planted,
202     blended_recall: blended / planted,
203     by_gate: byGate,
204   };
205 }
206 
207 // ── Measure the core's recall against the frozen Wave-3 baseline (by hash) ───────────────────────────
208 /**
209  * Run the evidenced core over the frozen fixture and measure its recall against the single-pass
210  * baseline LOADED BY HASH (Wave-3 frozen artifact), broken out BY SOURCE GATE and BY CLASS (incl. the
211  * CBS class). The crit-1 accuracy number is attributed to accuracy gates only (I5); CBS recall is
212  * reported as a measured ceiling (I1); independent origins come from the shared module (Wave 2).
213  *
214  * @param {{ baselineHash:string, gates?:string[] }} o
215  *   - baselineHash: the frozen Wave-3 baseline hash the caller PINS (load-by-hash; a wrong/regenerated
216  *     baseline throws — a later wave never measures against the wrong baseline).
217  *   - gates: which core gates are active (default G1+G2; G2 originates no catch on real planted
218  *     defects — no defect is detectable_by G2, I5 — so it appears only as precision).
219  * @returns {object} the measured recall report.
220  */
221 export function measureRecall({ baselineHash, gates = ['G1', 'G2'] } = {}) {
222   if (typeof baselineHash !== 'string' || baselineHash.length === 0) {
223     throw new TypeError('measureRecall requires the frozen baselineHash to load by (Wave-3 load-by-hash)');
224   }
225   const baseline = loadBaselineByHash(baselineHash); // loads + verifies the frozen Wave-3 baseline
226   const { defects } = loadFixture();
227   const recallDefects = defects.filter((d) => RECALL_CLASSES.includes(d.class));
228   const planted = recallDefects.length;
229 
230   const useG1 = gates.includes('G1');
231 
232   // Per-defect catch list, each catch tagged with the gate(s) that caught it. (G2 catches nothing over
233   // real planted defects — no defect is detectable_by G2; I5: it injects no new external bits.)
234   const catches = [];
235   for (const d of recallDefects) {
236     const caughtGates = [];
237     if (useG1 && g1Catches(d)) caughtGates.push('G1');
238     if (caughtGates.length) catches.push({ id: d.id, class: d.class, gates: caughtGates });
239   }
240 
241   const attribution = attributeRecall(catches, { planted });
242 
243   // Breakout BY CLASS (incl. the CBS class explicitly).
244   const byClass = {};
245   for (const cls of RECALL_CLASSES) {
246     const inClass = recallDefects.filter((d) => d.class === cls).length;
247     const caughtInClass = catches.filter((c) => c.class === cls).length;
248     byClass[cls] = {
249       planted: inClass,
250       caught: caughtInClass,
251       recall: inClass ? caughtInClass / inClass : 0,
252     };
253   }
254 
255   // Gap-closure vs the single-pass baseline (accuracy-attributed; crit-1): of the defects the single
256   // pass MISSED, how many an accuracy gate now catches. The denominator is the baseline's frozen
257   // single-pass miss count — i.e. G is a fraction of THIS (crit-1).
258   const singlePassMisses = baseline.gap_closure_denominator.single_pass_misses;
259   const accuracyCaughtIds = new Set(
260     catches.filter((c) => c.gates.some((g) => ACCURACY_GATES.includes(g))).map((c) => c.id),
261   );
262   const closed = recallDefects.filter(
263     (d) => d.single_pass_caught === false && accuracyCaughtIds.has(d.id),
264   ).length;
265 
266   // Independent origins via the SHARED module (the sole counter, Wave 2). The default core is ONE
267   // same-lineage reviewer family ⇒ exactly ONE origin ⇒ it does NOT meet the ≥2 quorum on its own.
268   const quorum = meetsQuorum([{ lineage: CORE_LINEAGE }], { staticFloor: STATIC_QUORUM_FLOOR });
269 
270   return {
271     baseline_hash: baselineHash,
272     gates: [...gates],
273     recall_class_planted: planted,
274     loop: {
275       caught: attribution.blended_caught,
276       planted,
277       recall: attribution.blended_recall,
278       by_class: byClass,
279       by_gate: attribution.by_gate,
280     },
281     accuracy: { caught: attribution.accuracy_caught, recall: attribution.crit1_accuracy_recall },
282     precision: { precision_only_caught: attribution.precision_only_caught },
283     crit1_accuracy_recall: attribution.crit1_accuracy_recall,
284     blended_recall: attribution.blended_recall,
285     gap_closure: {
286       single_pass_misses: singlePassMisses,
287       closed,
288       fraction: singlePassMisses ? closed / singlePassMisses : 0,
289     },
290     // I1/I2 honesty: report CBS recall as a MEASURED CEILING, never a closed result.
291     cbs: { recall: byClass[CBS_CLASS].recall, ceiling: true, stamp: CBS_CEILING_STAMP },
292     quorum,
293     cross_model: false, // default same-lineage core: no cross-lineage origin (I3). Enhanced = Wave 7.
294     baseline_recall: {
295       overall: baseline.single_pass.recall,
296       by_class: {
297         ordinary: baseline.single_pass.by_class.ordinary.recall,
298         [CBS_CLASS]: baseline.single_pass.by_class[CBS_CLASS].recall,
299       },
300     },
301   };
302 }
